DILG BAGONG PIUPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://wwudi\g,gpy.ph s. 202L OPINION NO. HON. FATIMA C. CANAMAQUE Municipal Mayor Municipality of Basay Province of Negros Oriental Dear Hon. Canamaque: This has reference to your letter dated May 31, 2023 seeking legal opinion from this Department regarding the Indigenous People Mandatory Representation in the locai legislative body of the Municipality of Basay, Province of Negros Oriental. Per your representation, the problem arose when the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of the province of Negros Oriental, in its Resolution No. 427, dated June 6, 2022, refused to declare operative the appropriation for one (1) Sectoral Representative (IP) under the office of the Vice Mayor. You then represented that one Mr. Rene F. Trono is the Sectoral Representative of the Indigenous People in the Municipality of Basay and that he has a Certificate of Affirmation. You mentioned that you appropriated funds for the function of his office under ordinance number 20-12-18, series of 2020 for the fiscal year 2021. However, this was excluded by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan as above-mentioned. You mentioned that Mr. Trono assumed office in 2022 and he tried to claim his salary and other benefits which already totaled to P351,917.41 as of January 19, 2023. However, your municipal accountant has denied his claim for the reason cited above. Despite of this, Mr. Trono continued his duty by attending the regular sessions of the Sangguniang Bayan of Basay and also attends committee hearings where he signed in committee reports. Thus, the request for legal opinion on the following issues: Is the continued attendance of Mr. Trono in committee hearings and I. regular/special sessions of the Sangguniang Bayan of Basay allowed and valid? 2. Is the local government of Basay liable for Mr. Trono's salaries and benefits despite the absence of an appropriation ordinance? 3. Are the related expenses of Mr. Tono in running the affairs of his office (travel, supplies, etc.) allowable? 4. Was the exception of the appropriation of an IP representative in the Local Sanggunian of Basay by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Negros Oriental ipso facto results in the non-existence of that office? As to the first query, we answer in the positive. "Matino, Mahusay, at Maaasahan" Trunkline: (02) 8876-3454



May it be respectfully informed that Sections 12 and 20 of NCIP AO No. 3, series of 2018 provides for the term of office and the grounds for disqualification of an IPMR before he can be considered removed or disqualified and we quote: "Section 12. Term of Office. The term of office of the IPMR in the local legislative councils shall be for a period of three (3) years and shall commence from the time of actual assumption to office and can be re-indorsed for another term by the ICCs/lPs constituents, but in no case shall the representative serve for more than two (2) consecutive terms, except in LGUs where a term rotation agreement has been reached by several IP groups limiting the holding of office to one term for every community. Xxxx" (Emphasis and underlining supplied) Section 20. Disqualification and Protest. A petition for disqualification or protest may be filed in any appropriate offices of the concerned region, and shall be treated liberally, with the technical rules of evidence applied only in suppletory character. In case of doubt, it shall be resolved in favor of the issuance of the COA. If the act complained of involves violation of customary laws, the matter shall be remanded to the community for dispute resolution. b. Grounds for petition for disqualification. 1. Those who are not qualified and who are disqualified under the local guidelines. 2. Those who are not qualified and who are disqualified under these guidelines (National Guidelines); 3. Commission of any of the prohibited acts under Section 21 ; 4. Analogous circumstances. c. Grounds for Protest I. Irregularity in the selection process; 2. Validity of the COA Xxxx" From the foregoing, the term of office of the IPMR in the sanggunian shall be three (3) years and in no case shall serve for more than two (2) consecutive terms, unless several IP groups have reached a term rotation agreement limiting the holding of said office to one term for each community. In the matter at hand, considering that Mr. Trono is the incumbent IPMR in the Municipality of Basay, and that nowhere in the letter is it stated that Mr. Trono has held said office for more than two consecutive terms or that he has been disqualified as the IPMR, his continued attendance in committee hearings and regular/special sessions of the Sangguniang Bayan of Basay remains allowed and valid. Consequently, he can only be validly removed from office, either by ICCs/lPs themselves pursuant to their authority to replace the selected IPMR at any time under Section 22 of the mentioned NCIP AO, or upon proper action ordering the IMPR's removal, disqualification or suspension from office. Thus, Mr. Trono may still hold office and attend committee hearings and sessions of the Sangguniang Bayan of Basay until the end of his term. Since the second and third queries are interrelated, we deem it proper to answer them in one (1) discussion. Page 2 of 4

In reply thereto, we invite your attention to Section 15 of NCIP AO No. 3, series of 2018 and Section 447 (b) of R.A. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991, viz: "Section 15. Compensation and Benefits. Compensation, benefits and other emoluments of the IPMR shall be the same with that of the reqular members of the concerned leqislative bodies as prescribed in R.A. 7160 and other applicable laws. Section 447. Powers, Duties, Functions and Compensation. - (b) The members of the sanqguniang bayan shall receive a minimum monthly compensation correspondinq to Salarv Grade twentv-four (24) as prescribed under R.A. No. 6758 and the implementing guidelines issued pursuant thereto: Provided, That, in municipalities in Metropolitan Manila Area and other metropolitan political subdivisions, members of the sangguniang bayan shall receive a minimum monthly compensation corresponding to Salary grade twenty-five (25)." (Emphasis supplied) Clearly, the compensation of the IPMR shall be the same with that of a regular member of the Sanggunian Bayan, which is a minimum monthly compensation corresponding to Salary Grade twenty-four. Corollary thereto, the IPMR shall receive his/her compensation in the same way as the regular sangguniang member as these compensation and benefits were clearly provided by law Thus, we are of the view that until the IPMR is validly removed from office, either by ICCs/IPs themselves pursuant to their authority to replace the selected IPMR at any time under Section 22 of the mentioned NCIP AO, or upon proper judicial action ordering the IMPR's removal or suspension from office, said IPMR should be given his compensation for services actually rendered and other benefits appurtenant thereto. As to the related expenses of Mr. Trono in running the affairs of his office (travel, supplies, etc.), the law does not mention of these expenses, and hence, such expenses should be borne by his compensation and benefits attached to his office as abovementioned. As to the final query, we also answer in the negative. Republic Act 8371 , otherwise known as the "Indigenous People Rights Act of 1991" was approved and signed into law on 29 October 1997. Said RA provides that the Indigenous Cultural Communities/lndigenous Peoples (ICCs/IPs) have the right to participate fully, if they so choose, at all levels of decision-making in matters which may affect their rights and lives through procedures determined by them as well as to maintain and develop their own indigenous political structures. Said law recognizes the policy of the State in affording the indigenous people communities' adequate representations in the local sanggunian at all levels. I Precisely, pursuant to Section 6, Rule IV of the Implementing Rules and Regulations of 8371 , it is mandated that the ICCs/lPs shall be provided mandatory representation in all policymaking bodies and in local sanggunians. ICCs/IPs representation shall be made proportionate to their population and shall have the same privileges as the regular members of the local sanggunians and/or policy making bodies. DILG Legal opinion No. 20 s. 2011, May 31, 2011. Page 3 of 4

On 16 August 2018, the NCIP again issued NCIP Administrative Order No. 3, series of 2018 prescribing national guidelines for the mandatory representation of Indigenous Peoples in the local sanggunians. Further, nowhere can we find in RA 8371 , its Implementing Rules and Regulations, and NCIP Administrative Order No. 3 series of 2018 a provision requiring an appropriation of an IP representative or prior acceptance by the local chief executive on the selected ICC/IP representative before the latter is allowed to assume as ex-officio member of the local sanggunian. It could never have been the intention of RA 8371 to give wide latitude of powers to the local sanggunian or the local chief executive to withhold their approval or the appropriation of their budget on their already selected ICC/IP representative thereby holding the decision of the ICCs/lPs hostage to their sole discretion.2 Thus, it cannot be stated that the IPMR office is ipso facto non-existent due to the inability of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Negros Oriental to appropriate funds in the Local Sanggunian of Basay, because the abovementioned office or representation is mandatory and granted by law. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, YAU ORITY OF THE SE ETARY: JUAN VICTOR R. LLAMAS Un secretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs O SELLNJVRULLLS-LRALLDnasm copy furnished: JUAN JOVIAN E.
